segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ חָצֵר שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — הַמַּכְנִיס מִתּוֹכָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, אוֹ מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לְתוֹכָהּ — חַיָּיב, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «a courtyard that was breached into the public domain,» and the breach was more than ten cubits wide, so that it cannot be considered an entrance, «one who carries» an object «from inside» the courtyard «into the private domain, or from the private domain into it, is liable,» as it ceases to be a private domain and is subsumed into the public domain. This is «the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.»

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מִתּוֹכָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים אוֹ מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לְתוֹכָהּ — פָּטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא כְּכַרְמְלִית.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis» disagree and «say:» One who carries «from inside» the courtyard «into the public domain, or from the public domain into it, is exempt, because its» legal status «is like» that of «a karmelit.» Although it ceases to be a private domain, it does not become a full-fledged public domain.

moves.summary: R' Eliezer: carrying from the breached courtyard to a private domain is liable
The Sages: carrying to/from the public domain is exempt; it is a karmelit

edges.about: whether a courtyard breached into the public domain becomes public domain (liability) or only a karmelit (exempt)

positions.claim: one carrying from the breached courtyard to a private domain or vice versa is liable; it has become public domain
carrying between it and the public domain is exempt, since it is like a karmelit
